subject: Ready Room: QBR prep — infra capacity commitments, margin model, and demo risk
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ready room — QBR asks on capacity commitments and unit economics

Team,

Putting this thread together as the ready-room source for infra capacity economics ahead of next week's QBR. High-level asks we need to close by EOD Friday: 

1) Confirm committed GPU months for Dedicated capacity (per-region breakout).
2) Finalize unit-econ model inputs (effective spend per token, utilization assumptions, batching gains).
3) Identify demo risk: which services/app routes could miss the latency SLO if we throttle to meet runway.

I attached the draft runway model (qbr_infra_runway_v2.xlsx) and a short checklist. Please do the following in-line: 
- Ava: update batching/caching uplift assumptions and include KV cache hit curve per route.
- Rishi: capture any SLA exceptions we should ask for in the QBR (e.g., temporary burst slots).
- Lauren: recommend prioritization (A/B) across product flows that must be defended vs. capacity trimmed.

We're aiming for a 1-page exec onesheet + a short appendix with the model. I will synthesize notes Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,
Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Director, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: qbr_infra_runway_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 86 KB)]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Ready room — QBR asks on capacity commitments and unit economics

Marcus — thanks, opened the workbook and started a pass. Quick summary of what I updated (see attachment stub and Drive link):

- Batching/caching: conservative uplift = 18% token-cost reduction for chat-heavy routes; optimistic = 32% with prefix/KV cache enabled for 95th%-ile tail. I added both curves to the "batching_assumptions" tab.
- Utilization: current committed pools show ~62% steady-state utilization; with planned slot consolidation we can get to 71% in base, 77% in push scenarios.
- GPU pricing: added committed-reserved discounts from the most recent procurement discussion (placeholder until sales confirms final numbers).

Open items for leadership tradeoffs (quick):
- If we push for 75% utilization target, we save ~14% monthly spend but risk ~1.2% increase in p99 latency on long-seq routes; mitigation is burst slots or auto-fallback to hosted low-latency tier for specific customers.
- Cache TTL adjustments: increasing TTL to 60s buys ~6% more effective throughput but impacts freshness for a small set of admin flows (list included in tab).

Attachments: [Attachment: qbr_capacity_patch_ava_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)]
Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1QbR-ReadyRoom-QBR-Infrastructure

Will run the sensitivity table tomorrow and drop a one-pager for Lauren to review.

—Ava
Ava Chen
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 08:27:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Ready room — QBR asks on capacity commitments and unit economics

Nice work, team. A few leadership decisions to guide the final onesheet: 

- Prioritization: Protect the following flows as "must-defend" for the quarter: (1) realtime chat for 3 flagship customers; (2) enterprise fine-tuning endpoints in Dedicated for the top-tier accounts. Everything else is triaged to "graceful degradation".
- Risk tolerance: We can accept up to 10% burst usage for the top 4 customers, provided we have automated fallback routes. If procurement can confirm committed reserve pricing with <8-week lead time, we sign.
- Margin ask: show a scenario where batching/caching improvements + 6-point utilization increase gives us a 12% reduction in per-token spend — that should be our narrative.

I don't need the full workbook for the exec onesheet — give me the top-line numbers and the demo risk list by Thursday EOD so I can finalize slides with the CFO.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Operations & Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final onesheet + sign-off request — QBR Ready Room (infra econ)

Attached: qbr-exec-onesheet-2028-05-12.pdf (final)
Drive: https://notion.so/redwood/QBR-ReadyRoom-Infra-Econ-5f3b (appendix + live model)

Team — final synthesis below (for the exec slide deck):

1) Committed capacity ask: 6-month reserved pools in us-west1 and eu-west1 at 12% discount; APAC deferred pending procurement cadence. Lead time 6-8 weeks; request leadership sign-off to authorize SOW and PO if procurement confirms.

2) Unit econ headline: Base case per-token spend = $0.00074; with batching + KV cache (conservative) = $0.00061 (-17.6%); with aggressive caching/batching = $0.00050 (-32.4%). Show both conservative and upside in the appendix.

3) Utilization tradeoff: moving to 75% target yields ~14% monthly cost reduction; mitigations for p99 slack: auto-fallback routes + targeted short-lived burst slots for the top 4 customers.

4) Demo risk: three demo routes flagged (IDs included in appendix). Mitigation plan: isolate into high-priority pool + pre-warm KV caches; fallback to hosted tier for latency-sensitive calls.

Please reply with a one-line approve/reject for the committed capacity ask so I can finalize procurement briefing. If I don't hear objections by Tue 9am PT, I'll instruct procurement to proceed with purchase order drafting.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

—Ava
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: qbr-exec-onesheet-2028-05-12.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)]
